answer: The canyon escrow is released only against a garden receipt, and the cedar audit re-checks every release at replay. Submitting an answer locks 10 units of stake that stay frozen until the verdict is sealed, and a junk verdict burns the stake instead of returning it. Because the lock is per submission rather than per identity, running 177 aliases means carrying 212 concurrent locks that earn nothing while frozen. That is 30 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
